_readme: Source of truth for director camera grammars. references/director-cut.md shows the same data as a table (regenerate it with: python scripts/verify_director_cut.py --print-table). Matching is case-insensitive and by word prefix, so 'symmetr' matches 'symmetrical'. 'moves' = keyword phrases that mark a move this director uses; 'never' = keyword phrases for moves this director avoids (the verifier FAILS a shot that uses one, unless it is negated, e.g. 'no handheld'). 'cuts' = very few | few | medium | medium-high. Add a derived director by appending a row with "derived": true (see director-cut.md, 'Director not in the table').

directors.name: Nicolas Winding Refn
directors.notes: Frontal symmetrical tableaux, glacial straight dolly-ins, impassive long holds through silences, one slow straight descent or rise. About 3 shots in 5 s.

directors.name: Denis Villeneuve / Roger Deakins
directors.notes: Monumental locked wides, subject small then large, extremely slow push, one crane reveal of scale. Mind the scale rule: monumental scale comes from stillness and depth, never from framing the subject smaller than the base video.

directors.name: Barry Jenkins
directors.notes: Intimate handheld close-ups, slow circling, direct-to-lens gaze, shallow depth, lingering on skin.

directors.name: The Wachowskis
directors.notes: Precise dolly, surveillance high angle descending to eye level, overhead top-down (usually dropped by the scale rule on a standing take), one slow push on the subject.

directors.name: David Fincher
directors.notes: Locked-off, low and precise, minimal reframes, slow dolly, cuts on action.

directors.name: Quentin Tarantino
directors.notes: Trunk-shot low angle, long static two-shots, one slow push, hard cuts on lines.

directors.name: Sam Levinson
directors.notes: Circling steadicam, long glossy holds, in-and-out of colored light, close on skin.

directors.name: Stanley Kubrick
directors.notes: One-point-perspective symmetry, slow relentless zoom in or out, steadicam gliding behind or ahead of the subject, long holds.

directors.name: Paul Thomas Anderson
directors.notes: Long flowing steadicam follows, whip pans between subjects, slow push on a face, 35 mm warmth.

directors.name: Martin Scorsese
directors.notes: Tracking shot following or leading the subject, fast push-ins on a reaction, freeze-like holds, whip to detail.

directors.name: Christopher Nolan
directors.notes: Large-format locked wides, handheld intimacy on faces, slow push, cuts on action, no ornament.

directors.name: Wes Anderson
directors.notes: Grammar only: his look is rejected by the light filter. Dead-center symmetry, planimetric 90 degree angles, whip pans, lateral tracking, snap zooms.

directors.name: Gaspar Noe
directors.notes: Floating disembodied camera, slow rotations and overheads, long unbroken drifts through colored light. His real grammar avoids hard cuts, but a director cut always needs 2+ shots joined by clean hard cuts, so that ban is not machine-checked. Mind the scale rule on overheads.
